turns.user_message: Can I take three days of PTO from Tuesday 15 September to Thursday 17 September 2026 — and can you open the request for me?
turns.final_answer:
PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance.

Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.

Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne.

PTO requests of any length are approved by the employee's direct manager.

Recommendation — not company policy: Your PTO balance as of 1 September 2026 is 13.5 days remaining, which covers your three-day request. You have 8 business days of notice, which exceeds the 5-day requirement. Submit the request in MosaicOne for Dana's written approval.

Recommendation — not company policy: HR ticket MOCK-HR-000007 has been created to track your time-off request.

Next steps:
- Dana will review and approve in writing

answer_blocks.text: PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance.
Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.
Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne.
PTO requests of any length are approved by the employee's direct manager.

Your PTO balance as of 1 September 2026 is 13.5 days remaining, which covers your three-day request. You have 8 business days of notice, which exceeds the 5-day requirement. Submit the request in MosaicOne for Dana's written approval.
HR ticket MOCK-HR-000007 has been created to track your time-off request.

citations.snippet: PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice.

PTO accrues monthly and is posted to the employee's MosaicOne balance on the first calendar day of each month. Accrual is not pro-rated within a month: an employee who is active on the posting date receives the full monthly posting for that month.

Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne. Verbal agreement, a message in chat and an email thread are all insufficient on their own: the approval must be recorded against the request so the audit trail is complete.

PTO requests of any length are approved by the employee's direct manager. Longer requests and requests overlapping a blackout period additionally require director approval, and the notice periods below come from the PTO & Holidays Policy.

tools.name: check_policy_compliance
tools.description: Evaluate one HR scenario against the policy rules deterministically: which requirements apply, which are met, which approvals the request needs and what to do next, every requirement citing the policy section that backs it. No model judgement is involved.

scenario.description: Which of the seven scenarios to evaluate.
scenario.title: Scenario

policy_topics.description: Advisory: topics the caller wants covered. Never changes a verdict.
policy_topics.title: Policy Topics

parameters.description: Scenario facts the engine cannot read from the record, e.g. destination_country, duration_days, start_date, days, amount_usd, category, transaction_date. Notice days are always computed by the engine from start_date against the data snapshot and any supplied notice value is ignored.
parameters.title: Parameters

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-4 result, or `{status: not_found}` for an unknown employee id.
output_schema.title: ComplianceOutput

tools.name: check_pto_balance
tools.description: The employee's PTO balance at the data snapshot: accrual rate, accrued and used days, pending requests, carryover and the computed remaining days, plus the blackout dates. A requested as_of later than the snapshot is echoed and answered from the snapshot.

as_of.description: An ISO-8601 date the caller cares about; echoed as requested_as_of.
as_of.title: As Of

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-6 result, or `{status: not_found}` — every field is optional for that reason.
output_schema.title: BalanceOutput

tools.name: create_mock_hr_ticket
tools.description: Open a mock HR ticket in one of the HR queues. Requires human confirmation: called without a valid one-time confirmation_token it returns status='confirmation_required' with a human_summary to show the user, and writes nothing. Never invent a token.

queue.description: Which HR queue the ticket belongs in.
queue.title: Queue

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-8 result, or the five-key `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` rejection on `isError`.
output_schema.title: TicketOutput

tools.name: draft_hr_email
tools.description: Draft an HR email to the employee's manager, skip level or an HR team. Requires human confirmation: called without a valid one-time confirmation_token it returns status='confirmation_required' and writes nothing. Never invent a token.

recipient_role.description: Who the draft is addressed to.
recipient_role.title: Recipient Role

key_points.description: The points to make, one per bullet.
key_points.title: Key Points

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-9 result, or the five-key `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` rejection on `isError`.
output_schema.title: EmailOutput

tools.name: get_policy_section
tools.description: Return the verbatim text of one section of a policy document, with its neighbours and siblings for context. Supply exactly one of heading_path or chunk_id. Neither is an error; if both are given, chunk_id wins and resolved_by says so.

heading_path.description: The ' > '-joined heading path, e.g. 'Accrual > Standard Accrual Rates'.
heading_path.title: Heading Path

include_neighbors.description: Also concatenate the previous and next sections into text.
include_neighbors.title: Include Neighbors

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-2 result, or `{status: not_found}` when the selector resolves to nothing.
output_schema.title: SectionOutput

tools.name: list_policy_documents
tools.description: List the HR policy documents in the corpus with their topics, sizes and effective dates. Call it to find a doc_id, or to say honestly what the corpus does and does not cover.

tools.name: lookup_benefits_status
tools.description: Benefits eligibility and current elections at the data snapshot, with the open-enrollment window. Eligibility is computed against the snapshot, not today's date.

plan_type.description: Filter the elections; 'all' returns them all.
plan_type.title: Plan Type

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-7 result, or `{status: not_found}` — every field is optional for that reason.
output_schema.title: BenefitsOutput

tools.name: lookup_employee_profile
tools.description: Look up one employee's synthetic HR profile: role, office, work arrangement, tenure at the data snapshot, manager and skip level. An unknown id returns status='not_found'.

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-5 record, or `{status: not_found}` — every field is optional for that reason.
output_schema.title: ProfileOutput

tools.name: search_policy_documents
tools.description: Semantic + lexical search over the 14 HR policy documents. Returns ranked chunks with the ids and heading paths a citation needs, each carrying the chunk's full text as well as a 320-character snippet, so a hit can be quoted without a second call; text is null on a hit marked quarantined, which carries its snippet only. Use get_policy_section for the sections AROUND a hit (include_neighbors) or for a section no search returned. topic prioritises one corpus topic; when the topic alone yields fewer than k hits or a single document, results are backfilled from the whole corpus.

query.description: The question, in the user's words.
query.title: Query

doc_ids.description: Restrict the search to these doc_ids.
doc_ids.title: Doc Ids

topic.description: Prioritise one corpus topic. When the topic alone yields fewer than k hits or a single document, results are backfilled from the whole corpus.
topic.title: Topic

min_dense_score.description: Minimum DENSE score (dense_score = 1 - cosine_distance). Applied to the full fused candidate list, then the top-k is taken from the survivors. Never applied to rrf_score, whose maximum is ~0.033.
min_dense_score.title: Min Dense Score

SearchHit.description:
One ranked chunk, carrying every field a citation needs (R2.5) and the chunk itself.

`text` is the stored chunk, clamped to `CHUNK_MAX_CHARS`; `snippet` stays the 320-character
display subset a citation shows a reader. It is `null` — and `quarantined` is `true` — for a
chunk the §7.4 injection shield has quarantined, because a chunk whose text gives the assistant
orders must not be readable in the model's own context.
SearchHit.title: SearchHit

output_schema.description:
The §8.4 tool-1 result. `k_source` records which of the three `k` inputs won.

`topic_backfilled` is `true` when at least one returned hit came from the unfiltered search the
soft `topic` filter runs underneath itself, and `backfill_reason` says what triggered it. They
move together: a widening that added nothing reports `false`/`null`, exactly as a search that
passed no `topic` does.
output_schema.title: SearchOutput

hits.text:
Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne. Verbal agreement, a message in chat and an email thread
are all insufficient on their own: the approval must be recorded against the request so the audit trail is complete.

A request that has been open for three business days without a decision escalates automatically to the skip-level manager, as described in the Manager
Approval Matrix. Escalation does not approve the request; it moves the decision to someone who is available to make it.

Requests longer than 15 consecutive business days additionally require director approval. Requests that overlap a declared blackout period require
director approval regardless of length. In both cases MosaicOne routes the request to the second approver automatically once the direct manager has
approved it, and the employee sees both decisions on the request record.
hits.snippet: Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne. Verbal agreement, a message in chat and an email thread are all insufficient on their own: the approval must be recorded against the request so the audit trail is complete.

hits.text:
PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of
advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence,
excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

The notice requirement exists so that a manager can rebalance work, not to create a barrier. A manager may waive the notice requirement for a request
that falls inside the window; the waiver is recorded in MosaicOne with a short reason, and People Operations reviews waivers quarterly to make sure the
exception has not become the rule.

Unforeseeable absences — a sudden illness, a family emergency, a transport failure that makes work impossible — are never held to the notice
requirement. The employee notifies their manager as early as they reasonably can, and the absence is entered in MosaicOne retroactively, against sick
time where the reason was illness and against PTO otherwise.

hits.text:
Hybrid employees assigned to a hub office work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by the team, not by the individual, so that
a team's onsite days overlap and the office time is actually collaborative; most teams anchor on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

A week containing a company holiday, approved PTO or approved travel reduces the requirement proportionally: an employee who works three days in a
holiday-shortened week is expected on site for two of them. The requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average in MosaicOne rather than week by
week, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem.

Managers are responsible for the requirement within their team. Persistent, unexplained non-attendance is a performance conversation, not a
disciplinary one, and People Operations expects the manager to ask what is getting in the way before escalating anything.

tools.name: check_policy_compliance
tools.description: Evaluate one HR scenario against the policy rules deterministically: which requirements apply, which are met, which approvals the request needs and what to do next, every requirement citing the policy section that backs it. No model judgement is involved.

scenario.description: Which of the seven scenarios to evaluate.
scenario.title: Scenario

policy_topics.description: Advisory: topics the caller wants covered. Never changes a verdict.
policy_topics.title: Policy Topics

parameters.description: Scenario facts the engine cannot read from the record, e.g. destination_country, duration_days, start_date, days, amount_usd, category, transaction_date. Notice days are always computed by the engine from start_date against the data snapshot and any supplied notice value is ignored.
parameters.title: Parameters

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-4 result, or `{status: not_found}` for an unknown employee id.
output_schema.title: ComplianceOutput

tools.name: check_pto_balance
tools.description: The employee's PTO balance at the data snapshot: accrual rate, accrued and used days, pending requests, carryover and the computed remaining days, plus the blackout dates. A requested as_of later than the snapshot is echoed and answered from the snapshot.

as_of.description: An ISO-8601 date the caller cares about; echoed as requested_as_of.
as_of.title: As Of

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-6 result, or `{status: not_found}` — every field is optional for that reason.
output_schema.title: BalanceOutput

tools.name: create_mock_hr_ticket
tools.description: Open a mock HR ticket in one of the HR queues. Requires human confirmation: called without a valid one-time confirmation_token it returns status='confirmation_required' with a human_summary to show the user, and writes nothing. Never invent a token.

queue.description: Which HR queue the ticket belongs in.
queue.title: Queue

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-8 result, or the five-key `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` rejection on `isError`.
output_schema.title: TicketOutput

tools.name: draft_hr_email
tools.description: Draft an HR email to the employee's manager, skip level or an HR team. Requires human confirmation: called without a valid one-time confirmation_token it returns status='confirmation_required' and writes nothing. Never invent a token.

recipient_role.description: Who the draft is addressed to.
recipient_role.title: Recipient Role

key_points.description: The points to make, one per bullet.
key_points.title: Key Points

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-9 result, or the five-key `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` rejection on `isError`.
output_schema.title: EmailOutput

tools.name: get_policy_section
tools.description: Return the verbatim text of one section of a policy document, with its neighbours and siblings for context. Supply exactly one of heading_path or chunk_id. Neither is an error; if both are given, chunk_id wins and resolved_by says so.

heading_path.description: The ' > '-joined heading path, e.g. 'Accrual > Standard Accrual Rates'.
heading_path.title: Heading Path

include_neighbors.description: Also concatenate the previous and next sections into text.
include_neighbors.title: Include Neighbors

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-2 result, or `{status: not_found}` when the selector resolves to nothing.
output_schema.title: SectionOutput

tools.name: list_policy_documents
tools.description: List the HR policy documents in the corpus with their topics, sizes and effective dates. Call it to find a doc_id, or to say honestly what the corpus does and does not cover.

tools.name: lookup_benefits_status
tools.description: Benefits eligibility and current elections at the data snapshot, with the open-enrollment window. Eligibility is computed against the snapshot, not today's date.

plan_type.description: Filter the elections; 'all' returns them all.
plan_type.title: Plan Type

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-7 result, or `{status: not_found}` — every field is optional for that reason.
output_schema.title: BenefitsOutput

tools.name: lookup_employee_profile
tools.description: Look up one employee's synthetic HR profile: role, office, work arrangement, tenure at the data snapshot, manager and skip level. An unknown id returns status='not_found'.

output_schema.description: The §8.4 tool-5 record, or `{status: not_found}` — every field is optional for that reason.
output_schema.title: ProfileOutput

tools.name: search_policy_documents
tools.description: Semantic + lexical search over the 14 HR policy documents. Returns ranked chunks with the ids and heading paths a citation needs, each carrying the chunk's full text as well as a 320-character snippet, so a hit can be quoted without a second call; text is null on a hit marked quarantined, which carries its snippet only. Use get_policy_section for the sections AROUND a hit (include_neighbors) or for a section no search returned. topic prioritises one corpus topic; when the topic alone yields fewer than k hits or a single document, results are backfilled from the whole corpus.

query.description: The question, in the user's words.
query.title: Query

doc_ids.description: Restrict the search to these doc_ids.
doc_ids.title: Doc Ids

topic.description: Prioritise one corpus topic. When the topic alone yields fewer than k hits or a single document, results are backfilled from the whole corpus.
topic.title: Topic

min_dense_score.description: Minimum DENSE score (dense_score = 1 - cosine_distance). Applied to the full fused candidate list, then the top-k is taken from the survivors. Never applied to rrf_score, whose maximum is ~0.033.
min_dense_score.title: Min Dense Score

SearchHit.description:
One ranked chunk, carrying every field a citation needs (R2.5) and the chunk itself.

`text` is the stored chunk, clamped to `CHUNK_MAX_CHARS`; `snippet` stays the 320-character
display subset a citation shows a reader. It is `null` — and `quarantined` is `true` — for a
chunk the §7.4 injection shield has quarantined, because a chunk whose text gives the assistant
orders must not be readable in the model's own context.
SearchHit.title: SearchHit

output_schema.description:
The §8.4 tool-1 result. `k_source` records which of the three `k` inputs won.

`topic_backfilled` is `true` when at least one returned hit came from the unfiltered search the
soft `topic` filter runs underneath itself, and `backfill_reason` says what triggered it. They
move together: a widening that added nothing reports `false`/`null`, exactly as a search that
passed no `topic` does.
output_schema.title: SearchOutput
